images.filename: Fort Union mechanic's corral in gingerbread (05cc8769-d491-43a5-aa7c-2a876396228f).jpg
images.caption:
Two juxtaposed images. On the top: The mechanic's corral at Fort Union featuring an arched doorway and windows made out of gingerbread, icing, and cinnamon, and wagon wheels made of orange slices. On the bottom: A similar view of the real mechanic's corral in the snow, showing the same arched doorway, windows, and wheels.)
A gingerbread rendition of the mechanic's corral at Forth Union. It's by far the most iconic view here at Fort Union and was re-created using home-made gingerbread for the wall, cinnamon sticks for the window lintels, dried orange slices for the wagon wheels, and royal icing/powdered sugar for the snow.
Keywords: Great NPS Bake Off; Food and Beverage

images.caption:
The ruins of an adobe fort in a desert landscape under a bright blue large sky. Wagons and wagon wheels are spread around the landscape.
Fort Union National Monument is located in New Mexico and was added to the Network in 2024. The fort was operating from 1851-1891. It played host to several companies of Buffalo Soldiers for five years. Troops and supplies from the fort were instrumental in the forced migration of indigenous peoples onto reservations. Slaves were present at the fort in the pre-Civil era when officers brought their household servants with them. The presence of the fort and the nearby Santa Fe Trail promoted the settlement of a diverse range of ethnicities in northern New Mexico in the post-Civil War years.
